item.title: [hackernews] Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen

item.title: [github_trending] vercel-labs/agent-desktop
item.description: agent-desktop is an Apache-2.0 npm package from Vercel Labs that lets AI agents read and drive desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux through the OS accessibility tree, skipping screenshots and pixel matching. It targets developers who want agents to operate conventional desktop software without maintaining a vision pipeline.

item.description: A Juejin post lists 32 Skills and 8 MCP servers that the author added to Claude Code, claiming all of them were tested and work, with a screenshot of the configured setup as evidence. It targets developers already using Claude Code who want its behavior tuned to concrete development tasks instead of running it bare. The individual Skill descriptions and setup notes live in the original article.

item.title: [infoq] 从英伟达到 Pika，硅谷巨头为何“反向借力”这个国产模型？
item.description: MiniMax opened the weights of its multimodal H3 model in August, drawing over 24 million downloads in a month and more than 300 public derivative models. Video firm fal trained H3 Max on top of it, Pika released H3 Flex on October 29 with fewer generation steps, and an Nvidia research team put out Open-H3-Regenerate-2K in late October alongside streaming-render and decoder work.

He advises newcomers to verify the app and official support, confirm fees, and check trade statements, and notes that one top-three brokerage has closed off waivers through a system upgrade.

item.title: [v2ex] [问与答] 用 claude code 和 codex，应该走什么订阅性价比最高？
item.description: A developer using dsv4 plus hermes for learning purposes wants to switch to an agent like Claude Code or Codex and is weighing subscription options. Having come across a goat plan offered through commandcode, they ask how such third-party subscriptions differ from buying official ones directly, and whether routing requests through commandcode is the only difference.

item.title: [infoq] Cilium 1.20 扩展了 Gateway API 并为 Kubernetes 开放了 eBPF 数据路径
item.description: Cilium 1.20 is out, moving Gateway API support from 1.4 to 1.6 with ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, and TCPRoute/UDPRoute, bringing HTTP authorization and non-HTTP traffic such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API. The release also exposes an extensible eBPF data path and advances sidecar-free mutual TLS; ListenerSets let app teams add listeners in their own namespaces while platform teams keep control of shared gateways.

item.title: [infoq] 微软推出 dotnetup：多版本管理更省心，安装方式却让开发者皱眉
item.description: Microsoft shipped a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager modeled on rustup and nvm that installs the .NET SDK and runtimes into the user's local data directory instead of Program Files\dotnet or /usr/share/dotnet. It resolves channels such as latest, lts or preview (or a major, minor or feature band) and reads the nearest global.json to keep builds deterministic. The default Windows-only everywhere mode rewrites system PATH and overrides machine-wide installs, including

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 如果 iPhone Duo 运行 iOS 18：一个 flutter 应用的适配尝试
item.description: Over a weekend the author adapted fluent-reader-lite, a five-year-old open-source Flutter RSS client built entirely with pre-iOS 26 Cupertino widgets, to the iPhone Duo form factor. Instead of following Apple's design guidelines, he borrowed a trick from WeChat Reading: rotating the status bar with preferredVerticalBarBehavior and placing it on the same row as the top navigation bar so the main UI fills the screen. The code is on GitHub for anyone curious about layout on wide or foldable screens

item.title: [v2ex] [分享发现] Google One 重新验证学生身份
item.description: A Google One user received a notice that their student status needs re-verification: the discount runs out unless verification is completed before December 5, 2026, so the Google AI Pro plan keeps its student price. Worth digging the email out of your inbox if you subscribe to Google AI Pro on a student discount, since missing the deadline means paying the regular rate.

item.title: [infoq] 谷歌宁愿少卖云算力，也要先把算力留给 Gemini：皮查伊罕见长访谈，披露 AI 自我改进与算力争夺内幕
item.description: In a Big Technology Podcast interview, Sundar Pichai said Gemini 4 Argon consumed nearly 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours, roughly triple Gemini 3.0 at the same point, and that compute supply cannot keep up. Google has been steering capacity to its AI research teams while the cloud unit gives up some short-term revenue, and he noted commit volume rose about 30% with rollbacks down a third in the four weeks after launch, making the share of AI-written code a less meaningful number.

Platform engineering lead Katelyn Lesse reports roughly 40-50% lower CPU usage and 10-20% better first-token latency. item.description: Nolan Lawson, a former performance program manager on Microsoft Edge, had an AI agent build the same Pokémon app in 12 JavaScript frameworks, all with Claude Opus 5.5 at high reasoning effort, then compared cost, token use and output quality. Hono+htmx came in at a median $2.67 versus $4.97 for Angular, with token consumption of 4.26 million against 9.76 million, roughly 2.3 times higher, raising the question of whether framework choices made for human developer experience still hold when agents

He also describes "adversarial review", where several Claudes critique each other and another judges the critiques, and calls "you are an expert in X" prompts a 2024 habit. His team built Claude Cowork in about a week and a

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin post works through a question that interviewers now ask: given that candidates are assumed to use AI, why should a company still hire you when AI already writes most of the code? The author contrasts this with interviews from two years ago, which still tested hand-written Promises and React Fiber internals, and argues the evaluation criteria have shifted. Useful for developers preparing for technical interviews right now.

item.title: [infoq] 从模型调用到任务交付：MaaS 如何走进 Agent 生产
item.description: Tencent Cloud upgraded TokenHub, a platform that puts multi-model access, call scheduling and enterprise governance in one place, with Day 0 onboarding for major models and compatibility with OpenAI and Anthropic protocols; TI-ONE, Agent Runtime and WorkBuddy were updated alongside it. Zou Hui, general manager of Tencent Cloud's MaaS product center, said per-million-token pricing has fallen from yuan to jiao and even fen as models spread through office scenarios.

item.title: [infoq] 从提效到扩能：AI 驱动小团队的能力突破与组织演进｜AICon北京
item.description: AICon Beijing runs December 18–19 at the Crowne Plaza Beijing Sun Palace, with 13 tracks spanning post-training, inference optimization, agent engineering, and agent evaluation and safety. Pan Chengbin, co-founder and CTO of SIMBOSS, speaks in the organizational restructuring track on how small teams move from efficiency gains to expanded capability, drawing on eSIM and multi-platform SDK work to discuss shifting roles and delivery ownership.

item.title: [infoq] 构建面向 Agentic 推理的下一代 LLM 推理引擎
item.description: TokenSpeed, presented by independent contributor Shang Xuchun at AICon 2026 Shenzhen, is an inference engine built for agentic workloads: rather than maximizing batch throughput, it targets the highest per-GPU throughput that still keeps each user above 70 TPS. On that basis it reports 9% lower end-to-end latency than TensorRT-LLM at batch size 1. The talk also covers a decoupled architecture, auto-parallel compilation and KV Cache reuse — useful for anyone tuning inference for multi-turn coding

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: The author writes up roughly half a month of using Codex after switching from Cursor: Cursor was what first made AI-assisted coding feel striking, while Codex comes across as a full agent that pushes tasks forward on its own rather than just a coding assistant. Aimed at developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt, or whether switching workflows is worth it.

item.title: [hackernews] WTF Ubuntu?
item.description: A blog post titled 'WTF Ubuntu?' says CVE-2026-98432, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code dating back to 2016, was fixed by Debian on October 16, while every supported Ubuntu release including LTS is still listed as vulnerable; Anthropic reportedly built a working exploit that yields root. The author is moving all his servers off Ubuntu and calls out Canonical's 'timely patches' marketing.

item.title: [github_trending] D4Vinci/Scrapling
item.description: Scrapling is a Python web-scraping framework that aims to handle everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl, with documentation hosted on Read the Docs. The repository also carries an MCP name tag, hinting it can be plugged into MCP-based tooling, and it is currently trending on GitHub. Developers who want one library that scales from scraping a single page to crawling a whole site are the target audience.

item.title: [36kr] 清华Nature子刊：上千智能体组网后自发站队，观点极化涌现
item.description: A Tsinghua study in a Nature sub-journal reports that when over a thousand agents are networked together, they spontaneously split into opposing camps and opinion polarization emerges. It speaks to anyone building multi-agent simulations or studying how large populations of agents behave collectively. Only the headline is available here; the linked paper isn't summarized and further experimental details aren't provided.

item.title: [juejin] Vibe Coding 时代：Vue 消失了还是 React 太强？
item.description: This article explores the shifting status of Vue and React in the era of Vibe Coding, where AI-assisted development is driven by mood and flow. The author analyzes why some believe Vue is fading while React grows stronger, noting that AI coding tools may favor React's ecosystem. It prompts readers to think about how frontend developers should choose their stack and whether Vue truly faces an existential threat as AI-assisted coding becomes mainstream.

item.title: [hackernews] Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace
item.description: A report flags a backdoor in the Claude Code extension for VS Code distributed through the Cursor Marketplace. The item only links to a Cursor security notice, and the linked page isn't summarized here, so affected versions, scope, and remediation aren't available. Developers who installed the extension from that marketplace should read the original advisory to check their exposure.

item.title: [hackernews] Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data
item.description: A GitHub issue filed against Postman claims that simply opening the app on a Mac triggered unexpected changes to the reporter's coding agents, while the title alleges it silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data. Postman typically holds API keys and request collections for whole teams, so unannounced behavior like this matters to backend and QA people who keep credentials there. The account so far comes from the reporter alone.

item.title: [zhihu] 清华毕业生 UCL 留学疑遭电诈，账户陆续转出数十万元，邮箱最新留言「我人平安，被诈骗了」，如何看待此事？
item.description: A Zhihu question describes a Tsinghua graduate studying at UCL who appears to have been hit by a telecom scam, with hundreds of thousands of yuan transferred out of the account in stages; the latest email from the person reads "I'm safe, I was scammed." The thread focuses on how overseas students should respond and where to seek help. The post is a question page, and no further case details are available here.

item.title: [github_trending] Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
item.description: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios is an MIT-licensed repo that turns a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio, shipping 49 agents and 74 skills along with 15 hooks and 14 rules. A coordination layer mirrors the hierarchy of a real studio, with roles divided across the agent team. It's aimed at game and tooling developers who want to orchestrate multi-role AI workflows, or who are curious how agent分工 and scheduling can be structured.

item.title: [github_trending] mattpocock/skills
item.description: Matt Pocock has published his personal agent skills, the set he uses daily for real engineering rather than vibe coding. They are deliberately small, composable, model-agnostic and meant to be forked and adapted, in contrast to process-owning approaches like GSD, BMAD and Spec-Kit that he says take control away from you. Aimed at developers who want a maintainable skill set for their coding agents.

item.title: [github_trending] thedotmack/claude-mem
item.description: claude-mem is a GitHub project that records everything an agent does during a session, compresses that history with AI, and injects the relevant parts back into later sessions so context carries over between runs. Its description says it works with Claude, which makes it relevant to developers running long, multi-session tasks who don't want to re-explain the background each time.

item.title: [hackernews] The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
item.description: A Hacker News submission argues that the circulating claim "Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen" is misleading, because the experiments that read raw weights and the ones that actually fix Qwen use completely different techniques. It's a useful caution for anyone tracking weight-editing or model-surgery claims: placing two results side by side can imply a causal link that isn't there.

item.title: [hackernews] An Italian farmer found some unknown seeds in his attic and planted them
item.description: Claudio Grossi, an Italian farmer, planted a handful of unidentified seeds he found in his attic, and a seven-eared stem came up. The seeds turned out to be an ancient grain that, per the piece, answers some modern problems. The available excerpt stops there: the specific variety and the problems it addresses aren't spelled out.

item.title: [hackernews] Postgres 19 is late because so many more bugs are being found now
item.description: A Hacker News post claims the Postgres 19 release is running late because far more bugs are being surfaced than in previous cycles. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available, so which components are affected and how long the delay lasts remain unknown.

item.title: [juejin] 手机到底有没有偷听我们？我抓包了 72 小时，抓到了真凶
item.description: A developer captured 72 hours of phone traffic and found zero microphone wake-ups at the hardware level, which weakens the "my phone is listening" theory. The uncanny precognition instead traces to public NAT spatio-temporal hypergraphs (ST-GNN), modern private set intersection (PSI), and on-device micro-model feature vectorization. Useful for engineers who want to understand how targeting actually works and where the privacy line sits.

item.title: [juejin] 2026编程圈很火的10个Skills
item.description: A Juejin post rounds up ten 'Skills' circulating in 2026 developer circles, meaning packaged skill sets for AI coding assistants rather than human expertise. Each Skill is a standardized workflow module meant to move an assistant from ad-hoc code generation to following a defined delivery process. It targets developers who want repeatable AI coding procedures instead of one-off prompts.

item.title: [juejin] 三年了，为什么 AI 应用还没爆发？
item.description: Starting from Meta’s “compute glut” narrative and the selloff in AI stocks, this piece asks why no breakout AI application has appeared after three years, when an AI-native Douyin, WeChat or Xiaohongshu might arrive, and whether the cycle repeats the dot-com bust of 2000. Useful for anyone tracking AI application-layer adoption and the surrounding investment story.

item.title: [github_trending] JustVugg/colibri
item.description: colibri is a pure-C inference engine for large mixture-of-experts models that tiers expert weights by temperature: hot experts on the GPU via CUDA or Vulkan, warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Since each token touches only a fraction of a several-hundred-billion-parameter MoE, it can run frontier open models on hardware you already own.

item.title: [github_trending] p-e-w/heretic
item.description: Heretic modifies language models without any training: strip censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy and more, with the project claiming it takes an afternoon on a gaming PC. Models are published through a Hugging Face org, and users can get help via its Discord and Matrix communities.

item.title: [juejin] 公司从 400 多人缩减到 100 多人，我开始重新思考程序员的未来
item.description: A personal essay on Juejin whose author watched their company shrink from over 400 people to just over 100, and uses that to rethink the future of programmers, touching on the situation of 35-year-old developers and the combined pressure of a weak market and AI. It is not a technical tutorial but one developer's read on an industry in retreat, useful for anyone weighing career plans.

item.title: [juejin] 我用 REA 逆向了付费颜色 APP，结果很意外！
item.description: The post first explains what reverse engineering is and introduces REA, an open-source project that has drawn attention on GitHub, then uses it with AI against a single-player Android game and a learning app. It suits readers who want a hands-on look at where AI-assisted reverse engineering actually lands, rather than a purely conceptual overview.

item.title: [github_trending] shiyu-coder/Kronos
item.description: Kronos is a foundation model for the language of financial markets, hosted on GitHub with a Hugging Face model page and a live demo. The repo displays stars, forks, and license badges, making its adoption status and license terms easy to gauge. For developers working on financial NLP or market language tasks, it's a practical starting point.

item.title: [github_trending] floci-io/floci
item.description: Floci is an open-source local cloud emulator pitched as an alternative to the AWS Local Emulator: you start it with a single docker compose up, with no account, no auth token and no feature gates, under the MIT license. It targets developers who want to exercise cloud-dependent code locally without touching a real cloud account or hitting paid tiers.

item.title: [github_trending] max-sixty/worktrunk
item.description: Worktrunk is a Rust CLI for managing Git worktrees, published on crates.io with docs at worktrunk.dev and dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0. It targets developers running several AI coding agents in parallel, so each agent can work in its own checkout without stepping on the others.

item.title: [juejin] 16 个超火的 DeepSeek Harness 插件，大肥鱼已经落后 N 个版本了。。。
item.description: A roundup of 16 popular plugins for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), grouped into three buckets: skill extensions, UI enhancements, and novelty builds. The listed plugins cover image recognition, browser control, multi-agent collaboration, and remote control from a phone. It is aimed at developers already running DSH who want more than the default capabilities, and it doubles as a rough map of which gaps the community is currently filling.
